editions.title: DoorDash buys Instacart; tech sell-off deepens over AI spending
editions.notification: DoorDash agrees to buy Instacart for about $17bn as AI spending worries rattle tech stocks.
editions.intro:
The biggest development is DoorDash's agreed deal to buy rival Instacart at $65 a share, a 26% premium, valuing the business at roughly $17 billion. The cash-heavy offer still needs regulatory and shareholder approval, and it would leave iPhone users with one fewer app-based grocery and delivery option. The deal lands amid a sharp slide in US tech shares, with the Nasdaq posting its worst month since March 2025.

That selloff is driven by fears about the roughly $800 billion that Meta, Alphabet, Oracle, Amazon and Microsoft are committing to spending in 2026. Intel fell 28% after warning of weaker PC demand, while Reddit dropped 29% after weak user numbers and complaints that Google's AI search is cutting its referral traffic. Reddit's CEO said Google's AI Mode does not drive meaningful traffic, and Alphabet's core ad growth slowed to its weakest pace in five quarters even as it kept capex guidance of up to $205 billion.

The AI nervousness also shows up in private markets. The Financial Times reports that OpenAI has cut its fundraising target by $10 billion, citing the AI selloff and Anthropic's forthcoming listing; Anthropic's IPO filing, meanwhile, shows $16.3 billion of first-half revenue alongside heavy losses. Apple, by contrast, retook the title of the world's most valuable listed company, supported by iPhone demand and its China AI rollout.

editions.title: Alphabet sheds $500bn as AI spending doubts hit Big Tech and Intel crashes
editions.notification: Alphabet loses $500bn in a day as AI spending doubts spread; Intel slumps on weak PC outlook.
editions.intro:
Investor patience with AI spending cracked this week. Alphabet lost just over $500bn in value after its quarterly update showed AI summaries in search weighing on advertising, with free cash flow negative by over $9bn. Amazon's free cash flow also swung deeply negative and its shares fell in after-hours trading, while Microsoft's shares barely moved despite 19% revenue growth. A global tech sell-off was reported to be deepening as the Nikkei and Wall Street opened lower.

Intel was the sharpest casualty. Its shares fell by roughly a quarter after third-quarter client chip revenue dropped and the company guided fourth-quarter revenue and earnings below expectations, blaming a memory shortage that is squeezing PC demand. Intel expects the PC market to shrink 12% this year. Reddit, meanwhile, said search referrals had fallen sharply and it will move to a logged-in-only experience, a direct example of how AI search is reshaping traffic.

Crypto was hit by a major security failure. Binance said an attacker drained hot wallets, with the affected amount put at about $6.3bn, and it pledged to cover losses from its SAFU fund and company money. Separately, reports that Nvidia's chief executive had ties to a Singapore businesswoman suspected by US intelligence of helping Beijing are unverified and have been strongly denied by Nvidia. Dealmaking continued, with DoorDash agreeing to buy Instacart for about $17bn and the FCC approving Amazon's Globalstar acquisition.

Amazon also fell after-hours on negative free cash flow, while Microsoft held up better. The reaction shows investors increasingly questioning the payoff from heavy AI spending.

top_stories.summary: Intel shares fell almost a quarter after client revenue fell and fourth-quarter guidance missed estimates by a wide margin. Chief executive Lip-Bu Tan blamed memory shortages and supply constraints, and forecast the PC market shrinking 12% this year. The stock had more than doubled earlier this year, so the drop is steep.

top_stories.summary: Attackers drained Binance hot wallets, with the affected funds put at around $6.3bn, and Tether and Circle froze stablecoins to help. Binance says the likely entry point was a compromised engineer's laptop and has pledged to cover all customer losses. The SAFU reserve covers only a fraction of the amount, so company funds will carry much of the cost.

editions.title: Alphabet's $500bn slide and Intel's crash rattle tech
editions.notification: Alphabet loses $500bn as AI spending doubts spread; Intel and Binance also reel
editions.intro:
Wall Street's tech earnings season turned sharply on Thursday as investors questioned how much AI spending will pay off. Alphabet shed just over $500bn in value, falling almost 13% to a six-month low, after its quarterly update showed AI summaries in search weighing on advertising revenue. Profits fell 25% and free cash flow was negative by more than $9bn, even though Google Cloud grew 103%. Amazon and Microsoft also reported strong top lines, but Amazon's free cash flow was deeply negative and its shares fell about 6% after hours, and a global tech sell-off was reported to be deepening.

Intel was the other major casualty. Its shares fell by almost a quarter after a steep drop in PC chip sales and a weak fourth-quarter forecast, with the chief executive blaming a memory-chip shortage and warning the PC market could shrink 12% this year. Datacentre and AI revenue rose 78%, but the company said it will likely not fully meet datacentre demand in the first half. Memory costs are a common thread, also hitting PC makers and smartphone shipments, which fell 20% in the third quarter.

Crypto and security stories dominated the rest of the day. Binance said an attacker drained hot wallets, with the affected funds now put at about $6.3bn; Tether and Circle froze stablecoin balances, and Binance has pledged to cover losses. Separately, a New York Times report alleging that Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang had ties to a Singapore businesswoman suspected of helping Beijing was met with Nvidia's denial. Several linked Nvidia items, including reported credit guarantees for Nscale, remain unconfirmed rumours.

editions.title: Binance hack, Alphabet rout and Intel slump rattle tech
editions.notification: Binance hit by a roughly $6.3bn crypto theft as Alphabet and Intel shares tumble on AI doubts.
editions.intro:
Markets and security were the dominant stories over the last 24 hours. Binance said an attacker drained its hot wallets, with the affected funds later put at about $6.3 billion. Tether and Circle froze significant stablecoin balances to help, and Binance has pledged to cover all losses from its SAFU fund and company money. The exchange blamed a likely entry point via a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, and withdrawals remain paused while it overhauls security. A crypto industry figure has said the bitcoin is probably unrecoverable, though that is an opinion rather than an official update.

Earnings reshaped the market mood. Alphabet lost just over $500bn in value after AI summaries in search weighed on ad revenue, even as Google Cloud grew 103%. Amazon's free cash flow turned sharply negative and its shares fell in after-hours trading. Intel dropped almost a quarter of its value after PC chip sales fell, with its CEO warning the PC chip market could shrink 12% next year. Taken together, investors are increasingly questioning how much AI spending will pay back.

Nvidia was the subject of several reports. The Information says it is in talks to guarantee billions of dollars of debt for Nscale's West Virginia data centre, which Anthropic plans to use under a deal worth about $45 billion. Separately, a New York Times report alleges US intelligence suspected a Singapore executive of acting for Beijing and linked her to Jensen Huang; Nvidia and the Chinese embassy have denied wrongdoing, and the claims rest on unnamed sources.

The SAFU fund covers only about a sixth of the amount.

editions.title: Apple's touchscreen Mac, Samsung's record profit and AI chip deals
editions.notification: Apple finally adds touchscreen MacBook Pros, and Samsung posts a record $80.5bn quarter.
editions.intro:
Apple has broken its long refusal to put touchscreens on Macs. The new 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro models use OLED XDR displays with touch input, and they start at $2,899 and $3,399 respectively. Pre-orders are open and shipping begins on 6 November. The launch is the first big product news under new chief executive John Ternus, and it comes with a premium price that buyers will notice.

The chip and memory sector dominated the day. Samsung reported a record third-quarter operating profit of KRW 107.4 trillion (about $80.5bn), driven by memory chips for AI data centres. Its executives said memory shortages will worsen in 2027 and persist into 2028, with long-term agreements covering 60 to 70% of capacity. Shares nonetheless slid, because profits narrowly missed some estimates and little was said about shareholder returns. Oracle, meanwhile, outlined a multi-vendor AI infrastructure push, deploying Nvidia Vera Rubin systems, AMD MI455X GPUs and Google TPUs from 2027.

On the deal front, the FCC approved Amazon's $11.5bn purchase of Globalstar, which strengthens Amazon's direct-to-device satellite ambitions and puts pressure on AST SpaceMobile. Separately, reports say OpenAI is considering buying Google TPUs, and Anthropic is weighing a retail tranche of up to 20% in its IPO. Both remain unconfirmed.

editions.title: Apple readies touchscreen MacBook Pro as Anthropic prospectus lands
editions.notification: Apple may finally put touch on the Mac this Wednesday, and Anthropic's IPO filing shows a $80.7bn half-year loss.
editions.intro:
Apple dominates the day's agenda. Reports citing Bloomberg's Mark Gurman say Apple will unveil redesigned 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro models on Wednesday 28 October, with touch-enabled OLED displays, which would be the first touchscreen Mac and a reversal of a long-held stance. Touchscreen models are reportedly premium additions, with the 14-inch starting at $2,899. Apple has also confirmed a refreshed iMac and entry-level MacBook Pro with the M6 chip, priced from $1,499 and $1,999, and it is acknowledging a small number of hinge-related screen failures on its $2,000 iPhone Duo, which has prompted questions about quality control on the new foldable.

The biggest financial story is Anthropic's public filing ahead of a US listing. The 335-page document shows a $80.7bn loss for the first half of 2026 on $16.2bn of revenue, roughly double its full-year 2025 loss, alongside heavy customer concentration and large data-centre costs. Valuations of $2 trillion or more are being discussed. Infrastructure news reinforced the AI chip story: Oracle plans to offer Google TPUs through its cloud from 2027, and OpenAI is reportedly considering buying TPUs, a move that would pressure Nvidia's position, although Nvidia is also gaining multi-gigawatt Vera Rubin deployments at Oracle.

Elsewhere, China's tech-heavy stocks have fallen sharply, with the STAR 50 down around 40% since June, while India's Jio Platforms rose 21% on its market debut. Microsoft is offering voluntary exit packages to roughly 60,000 staff, and it reports earnings this week.

top_stories.title: Apple set to unveil touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro on Wednesday
top_stories.summary: Citing Bloomberg, reports say Apple will show redesigned 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros with touch-enabled OLED screens on 28 October. If confirmed, it would be the first touchscreen Mac and a clear break from Apple's previous position.

top_stories.title: Anthropic's IPO filing reveals $80.7bn half-year loss
top_stories.summary: The 335-page prospectus shows $16.2bn in revenue and an $80.7bn loss in the first half of 2026, with heavy customer concentration and data-centre costs. Expected valuation is $2 trillion or more, making it a major test for AI listings.

top_stories.title: Oracle brings multiple AI chip vendors into one cloud
top_stories.summary: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure is deploying Nvidia Vera Rubin, AMD MI455X, Intel Diamond Rapids and Google TPUs from 2027. The move positions Oracle as a multi-vendor AI infrastructure hub and is a notable first for TPUs outside Google's own cloud.

top_stories.title: OpenAI reportedly plans to buy Google TPUs
top_stories.summary: According to The Information, OpenAI intends to buy Google's AI chips, deepening ties despite rivalry. Terms are undisclosed, but the move could pressure Nvidia's dominance in AI accelerators.

top_stories.title: Jio shares jump 21% on India market debut
top_stories.summary: Jio Platforms opened at ₹1,358 against a ₹1,119 IPO price, valuing it at about $131.9bn. The listing is one of India's largest and makes it the country's second most valuable listed company after Reliance.

top_stories.title: Chinese tech markets lose trillions in AI race
top_stories.summary: The STAR 50 is down about 40% since June and Bloomberg estimates $2.4tn has been wiped from Chinese stocks since May. Weak profits, soft consumer demand and fears of further US tech bans are cited, with the Party plenum next in focus.

top_stories.title: Apple acknowledges iPhone Duo screen failures
top_stories.summary: Apple says a small number of its $2,000 foldable iPhone Duo have inner-display problems, which iFixit links to the hinge. Customers are being directed to AppleCare for replacements, though the company has not disclosed the cause.

rumour_watch.note: Credible: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman is a strong source, and a follow-up report puts pricing and an invitation-only hands-on in Los Angeles on the same date, so the launch looks likely.
Weak: a one-line Digitimes headline with no detail on volumes or timing; treat as unconfirmed until a second source appears.
Low credibility: a feed summary at 20% citing a secondhand report of relaxed quality checks and a refused warranty claim, with no Apple response.
Moderately credible: The Information is well-sourced, and OpenAI has posted a TPU-optimisation job, though financial terms are unknown.

stocks_to_watch.name: Apple
stocks_to_watch.note: Touchscreen MacBook Pro expected Wednesday, plus M6 Mac refreshes, outweigh the iPhone Duo screen concerns.

stocks_to_watch.name: Nvidia
stocks_to_watch.note: Vera Rubin deployments at Oracle help, but OpenAI's reported TPU purchase and Oracle's TPU plans add competitive pressure.

stocks_to_watch.name: Alphabet
stocks_to_watch.note: TPU wins at Oracle and possibly OpenAI strengthen the case for Google's custom AI chips.

stocks_to_watch.name: Oracle
stocks_to_watch.note: Positions Oracle Cloud as a multi-vendor AI infrastructure platform, including TPUs from 2027.

stocks_to_watch.name: Amazon
stocks_to_watch.note: FCC approval of its $11.5bn Globalstar deal clears a path to a direct-to-device satellite rival to SpaceX.

stocks_to_watch.name: AST SpaceMobile
stocks_to_watch.note: Slipped after Amazon's Globalstar approval created a stronger competitor, and shares are down 29% over the month.

in_brief.line: Microsoft offers voluntary exit packages to about 60,000 eligible staff in the US, India, Canada and the UK ahead of earnings.
OpenAI says an internal model disproved the Exponential Time Hypothesis, with an independent review led by three academics.
South Korea's Fair Trade Commission fines Samsung about 20bn won over gaming performance claims on older Galaxy phones.
Australia's House passes digital duty of care bill, which would ban emotional-intimacy features on AI chatbots.
Researchers find Alibaba's Qwen 3.8 models sometimes route requests to Alibaba Cloud servers, in a finding Cohere has a stake in.
Pokémon Unite will shut down on 23 March 2027 on mobile and Switch, with a final update on 12 November.
Jay-Z confirmed as headliner for the Apple Music Super Bowl LXI halftime show on 14 February 2027.
AT&T's $177m data breach settlement moves toward payouts, with over 4.9 million claims filed.

Finance.title: Tech rout hits AI giants as AI spending doubts mount
Finance.notification: Tech stocks slump as doubts over AI spending deepen; Apple retakes the top spot from Nvidia.
Finance.summary:
A sharp sell-off in technology shares has dominated markets as investors question the cost of the AI build-out. Alphabet fell more than 12% in a single session, its worst day on record, and Intel dropped nearly 29% after a weak forecast. The Nasdaq 100 had its worst month since 2025, and Apple reclaimed the title of the world's most valuable listed company from Nvidia.

The pattern runs across regions. Amazon shares fell after it flagged about $220bn of 2026 capital spending, while the Kospi and Nikkei both closed down more than 2%, led by chipmakers. Europe's STOXX 600 eased on Friday as its tech index fell. Money markets are also watching central banks, with the Bank of Japan holding at 1.25% and signalling further tightening, while the ECB and Fed paused.

In Britain, the story is more about businesses under pressure: Poundland faces possible administration with about 12,000 jobs at risk, and Volkswagen-style cost pressures are echoed in a squeeze on household incomes. Crypto markets were also rattled by a $6.3bn hack at Binance, which investigators link to North Korea.

highlights.label: US
highlights.text: Alphabet fell over 12%, its worst day on record, while Amazon slid on heavy AI spending. Apple overtook Nvidia as the most valuable listed firm.

highlights.label: UK
highlights.text: Poundland is at risk of administration, with 12,000 jobs in danger. Stores remain open for now, and some retailers have bid for parts of the business.

highlights.label: Europe
highlights.text: France's economy shrank 0.1% in the third quarter and inflation rose to 3.4%. Economists see a possible technical recession ahead.

highlights.label: Asia
highlights.text: The Bank of Japan held at 1.25% in an 8-1 vote, with one member calling for a hike to 1.5%. Markets expect a December rise.

highlights.label: Markets
highlights.text: The Kospi closed down 3.48% and the Nikkei fell 2.12% as chipmakers led losses on AI spending concerns.

highlights.label: Crypto
highlights.text: Investigators link the $6.3bn Binance hack to North Korea's Lazarus Group. About 80% of the stolen assets are said to be secured.

points.text: AstraZeneca beat forecasts with core EPS of $2.79 against $2.62 expected, helped by Imfinzi and Tagrisso, and reaffirmed guidance.
NatWest posted flat third-quarter pre-tax profit of £2.2bn, the weakest growth among major UK banks, and its shares fell.
The IFS says UK household incomes will grow only about 2% over the 2020s, the weakest rate on record.
Volkswagen posted a €5.86bn operating loss, its worst quarter in over a decade, and plans to cut about 100,000 jobs.
Tesco agreed to sell its Czech and Slovak businesses to Ahold Delhaize for €1.7bn and will return more capital to shareholders.
About 91% of Monte dei Paschi voters rejected the defence plan against Intesa Sanpaolo's takeover bid.

World.title: Tech sell-off, Gulf war and US midterms weigh on markets
World.notification: Alphabet loses $500bn in a day as AI jitters spread, while Gulf tensions push oil higher
World.summary:
Alphabet's record one-day fall of more than 12% led a tech sell-off, after third-quarter results missed forecasts and investors questioned heavy AI spending and whether AI could erode search. Amazon and Intel results added to the pressure, while Microsoft rose after its own figures. The sell-off came alongside a $6.3bn hack at Binance, which half-frozen funds and North Korean links make a major crypto story.

The Iran war remains the backdrop for markets and politics. Tankers were reportedly hit in the Strait of Hormuz, and oil climbed. In the US, the midterms are four days away, with Trump cancelling and then reinstating rallies and a Senate race in Alaska drawing federal subpoenas. In Europe, Spain's snap election has been reshaped by a deadly rail crash, Lagarde's early exit from the ECB has opened a succession race, and Poland's constitutional court stand-off has turned into a riot-police confrontation. In Asia, the Bank of Japan held rates but signalled further hikes, lifting the yen.

For investors, the mix of AI capital-spending worries, energy supply risk and a possible renewed US offensive on Iran points to continued volatility.

highlights.label: US
highlights.text: Alphabet's record $500bn one-day loss followed weak results and AI spending worries; Microsoft rose after its own report.

highlights.label: US
highlights.text: Trump reinstated Kansas and Iowa rallies after first cancelling them, with the midterms four days away.

highlights.label: UK
highlights.text: Andy Burnham said he is open to a slavery apology but ruled out reparations ahead of a Commonwealth summit.

highlights.label: UK
highlights.text: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood is expected to unveil settlement reforms next week, with ministers divided over the 15-year wait.

highlights.label: Europe
highlights.text: Spain's snap election is reshaped after a rail crash killed at least 69 people, adding pressure on Sánchez over safety.

highlights.label: Asia
highlights.text: The Bank of Japan held rates steady and signalled further rises, lifting the yen and pressuring Japanese bond markets.

points.text: Binance's $6.3bn hack is among the largest crypto thefts on record; North Korean links are suspected but unclaimed.
Iran says several tankers hit mines near Hormuz; the Pentagon puts the war death toll at 23.
Senator Chris Murphy called reported US plans to restart the Iran war 'insane'; no final decision has been made.
Riot police confronted protesters outside Poland's constitutional court after judges were suspended.
Christine Lagarde is leaving the ECB early, sparking a succession race and speculation ahead of France's election.
France braces for a third weekend of protests, with 70,000 security personnel deployed on 31 October.

Tech.title: Tech stocks slide as AI spending fears deepen
Tech.notification: Tech shares slump again as AI spending worries grow. Intel and Reddit lead the falls. Here is what is driving the sell-off.
Tech.summary:
US tech shares fell for a second straight session as investors questioned the hundreds of billions being spent on AI. Intel dropped sharply after weak PC demand and a cash-burn warning, while Alphabet slipped further after a steep plunge and Reddit fell heavily after weak user figures and concerns about Google's AI search hitting referral traffic. The Nasdaq had its worst month since March 2025 in October, although it is still up over the past year. Around $800bn of 2026 spending by Meta, Alphabet, Oracle, Amazon and Microsoft is now under the microscope.

Investor unease is spreading beyond Wall Street. Reports of a global tech sell-off, with Japan's Nikkei falling, and reports that OpenAI has cut its fundraising target by $10bn point to a cooling mood around private AI valuations. Alphabet's core advertising growth slowed to its weakest pace in five quarters, yet it kept its capital spending outlook, sharpening the question of when returns will arrive.

Not all the news is gloomy. Apple has retaken the top spot as the world's most valuable listed company, Amazon's AWS is growing close to 40%, and Samsung and Tokyo Electron posted strong AI-linked profits. The split is clear: AI infrastructure demand is strong, but the cost and payback of the build-out are now being tested.

highlights.label: Intel
highlights.text: Shares fell over 20% after a weak fourth-quarter outlook, blamed on memory shortages hurting PC demand. The PC market is seen shrinking 12% this year.

highlights.label: Reddit
highlights.text: CEO Steve Huffman says Google's AI Mode does not drive traffic. Reddit will require logins, with tests starting in non-US markets in Q4.

highlights.label: Nvidia
highlights.text: Nvidia is reportedly in talks to guarantee billions in debt for Nscale, tied to a $45bn Anthropic compute deal. Nothing is signed yet.

highlights.label: DoorDash
highlights.text: DoorDash agreed to buy rival Instacart at $65 a share, about $17bn. The deal still needs approvals and would leave users with one fewer delivery app.

highlights.label: Anthropic
highlights.text: Anthropic is reportedly SpaceX's biggest customer, accounting for 34.5% of its third-quarter revenue, ahead of the US government.

highlights.label: Samsung
highlights.text: Samsung posted record Q3 operating profit of 107.44 trillion won, driven by chips, while its devices division made a loss.

points.text: Nvidia would hold three roles in the Nscale chain: chip supplier, equity investor and debt backer.
The FT reports OpenAI cut its fundraising target by $10bn, citing the AI selloff and Anthropic's forthcoming listing.
Apple has overtaken Nvidia as the world's most valuable listed company, closing at $344.63 on 30 October.
Global smartphone shipments fell 20% in Q3 to 254.7m units, the weakest third quarter since 2013, per Omdia.
China dismissed reports that a suspected spy targeted Nvidia's Jensen Huang, calling them groundless speculation.

Fashion.title: Luxury and fashion: Gucci's retail reset, Capri and couture
Fashion.notification: Gucci opens a new Paris flagship concept as Capri lifts its outlook and Versace returns to couture.
Fashion.summary:
Gucci's new store concept has opened on Avenue Montaigne in Paris, the first of a rollout with London, Shanghai and Chengdu due by year-end. Chief executive Francesca Bellettini says the format is built to outlast individual creative directors, while Kering's turnaround under Luca de Meo involves closing hundreds of underperforming stores.

Capri Holdings had a better quarter than expected. Revenue beat company and analyst forecasts, shares rose sharply, and the group said it expects a return to growth in the second half of the fiscal year. Michael Kors Americas fell 11%, while Jimmy Choo Americas rose 24%. Versace's return to haute couture in January 2027 adds to a wider push by houses such as Hermès and Celine into couture, which analysts see as a way to protect exclusivity and pricing.

Sportswear was also in focus. Adidas reported record third-quarter sales of €7.3 billion and raised its 2026 outlook, with direct-to-consumer sales growing strongly, while Puma's sales slowed less than expected as its partnership with Anta advances. The Dries Van Noten leadership change and Mbappé's China controversy add to a busy week for the sector.

highlights.label: Gucci
highlights.text: The new Avenue Montaigne store concept is the start of a rollout, with London, Shanghai and Chengdu due by year-end.

highlights.label: Capri
highlights.text: Revenue, operating income and EPS beat expectations, and buybacks continued with $721 million left on the programme.

highlights.label: Adidas
highlights.text: Record Q3 sales of €7.3bn and a raised 2026 outlook, with direct-to-consumer sales up 17% as wholesale was limited.

highlights.label: Couture
highlights.text: Atelier Versace returns to the couture calendar in January 2027, with Hermès also debuting and Celine reportedly exploring it.

highlights.label: Dries Van Noten
highlights.text: Adrian Ward-Rees, from Moncler Grenoble, becomes president on 1 December as the house accelerates retail expansion.

highlights.label: Resale
highlights.text: The RealReal grew Q3 revenue 19% to $206m and raised full-year guidance, though shares are down 28% this year.

points.text: Puma's sales slowed by less than analysts expected, and its partnership with Anta, which took a stake earlier this year, is advancing.
Bloomberg's column says Mbappé's China comment hurt Western partners On Holding and Dior, though the impact is unlikely to last.
Business of Fashion looks at the race among luxury houses to recruit top salespeople, some earning around $1m a year.
Carter's restructures its leadership, hiring Maria Gemzell from H&M as chief product officer, with changes aimed at being more consumer-centric.
Carter's Q3 operating income more than doubled to $55.8m, but it will moderate its revenue outlook because of consumer pressure.
Trent, behind Westside and Zudio, saw shares jump after rising quarterly profits and sales, pointing to resilient Indian value fashion demand.
